_meta.description: Document-rules config for posh_complaint — Complaint under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 to Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) [≥10 employees] or Local Complaints Committee (LC) [unorganised / <10 employees].
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Confidentiality protection S.16 paramount. Vishaka heritage cite mandatory.

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {complainant_name}, the Aggrieved Woman / Complainant herein, do hereby verify under solemn affirmation that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above complaint are true and correct to my personal knowledge. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed. I invoke the confidentiality protections under Section 16 of the Act.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Complainant

promptInstructions: Draft a complaint under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 — 'POSH Act' / 'SH Act'. Legislation traces lineage to Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) 6 SCC 241.

MANDATORY: Caption 'CONFIDENTIAL' on every page. Section 16 of the Act mandates confidentiality of the woman's identity, contents of complaint, inquiry proceedings, recommendations. Disclosure can lead to penalty under S.17.

Forum: ICC (Internal Complaints Committee — workplace with ≥10 employees, mandatory under S.4) OR LC (Local Complaints Committee — district level for workplaces with <10 employees / unorganised sector / where complaint against employer himself, S.6-7).
Para 1: Parties — anonymise where appropriate; do NOT publish in any extra-committee forum.
Para 2: Filed by self (S.9(1)) OR by authorised person under Rule 6 of POSH Rules 2013:
- Where woman is unable owing to physical incapacity — by relative or friend or co-worker or officer of NCW/SCW with written consent of woman;
- Where woman is unable owing to mental incapacity — by special educator / qualified psychiatrist / guardian / authority where she is receiving treatment / co-worker, with consent of guardian;
- Where woman has died — by legal heir.

Para 3: Workplace — definition S.2(o) is BROAD: includes private / public sector workplaces; departments under Government; hospitals / nursing homes; sports institutes; places visited by employee during course of employment ('extended workplace'); dwelling place for domestic workers; unorganised sector.
Para 4: Aggrieved woman — defined S.2(a): includes any woman, of any age, whether employed or not, who alleges sexual harassment by respondent.
Para 5: Respondent — defined S.2(m).
Para 6: Nature of sexual harassment — S.2(n) categories:
(i) Physical contact and advances;
(ii) Demand or request for sexual favours;
(iii) Making sexually coloured remarks;
(iv) Showing pornography;
(v) Other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature.
PLUS circumstances S.3(2):
(a) Implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment;
(b) Implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment;
(c) Implied or explicit threat about present or future employment;
(d) Interference with her work or creating intimidating / offensive / hostile work environment;
(e) Humiliating treatment likely to affect health or safety.
Para 7: Detailed chronology — date, time, place, exact words / acts. Avoid generalisations.
Para 8: Witnesses (if any) — name and what they witnessed.
Para 9: Documentary / electronic evidence — emails, WhatsApp screenshots, CCTV, recordings, prior complaints.

Para 10: Limitation — S.9(1) — 3 months from the date of incident; for series, 3 months from last incident. Committee may extend by further 3 months (proviso to S.9(1)) for reasons recorded in writing. Where extension sought, give reasons.

Para 11: Interim relief — S.12 read with Rule 8 POSH Rules: (a) transfer of aggrieved woman or respondent to another workplace; (b) grant of leave up to 3 months in addition to leave otherwise entitled; (c) restraining respondent from reporting on her work performance or supervising; (d) any other relief.

Para 12: Final relief — S.13 + Rule 9: (a) action per service rules / Standing Orders; (b) deduction of compensation from respondent's salary (S.13(3)(b)); (c) payment of compensation as per S.15 factors (mental trauma, loss of career, medical expenses, income & status of respondent, lump sum or instalments); (d) criminal action under BNS [where conduct also amounts to BNS S.74-79 (insult, voyeurism, stalking) or BNS S.63 (rape) etc.].
Para 13: Confidentiality — S.16 invoked. Penalty for breach S.17.

Para 14: Caution against malicious complaint — S.14: if Committee concludes complaint is malicious AFTER inquiry, action against complainant per service rules. NOTE: Inability to prove DIFFERS from malicious complaint; mere failure of evidence does NOT make complaint malicious.
Para 15: Right to appeal — S.18: appeal to court / tribunal per service rules within 90 days of recommendation.
Para 16: Inquiry timeline — S.11(4): completion within 90 days. Report to employer within 10 days of completion (S.13(1)).
Para 17: Where conduct also constitutes a crime under BNS — woman may simultaneously file FIR; POSH Committee does NOT bar criminal action.
Annexures: Identity proof; documentary evidence; witness list; medical / psychological reports if any.
Verification on solemn affirmation.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Constitution of LC at district level
Complaint of sexual harassment — substantive provision
Conciliation (at request of woman; not where settlement is monetary basis under threat)
Malicious complaint — action against complainant only on inquiry finding

sections.description: Persons who may file complaint where woman is unable / deceased

sections.description: Assault or use of criminal force with intent to outrage modesty (was IPC 354)
Assault with intent to disrobe (was IPC 354B)
Word, gesture or act intended to insult modesty (was IPC 509)

filing_checklist: Authorisation letter if filed by representative (Rule 6 categories)
No court fee (POSH proceedings are not court proceedings)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: complainant_name and complainant_age must not be empty
filed_by_self_or_authorised must be selected (with authorised_filer_details if not self)
incidents_dates and incidents_places must not be empty
nature_of_harassment must have at least one selected
limitation_position must not be empty — flag if > 3 months without reasons; flag if > 6 months as out of jurisdiction
final_relief_sought must have at least one option selected
If committee_type = local_committee_district, workplace_name must not be required (LC for workplaces <10 emp / unorganised)
Court level limited to ICC or LC
key_citations: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) 6 SCC 241 — Vishaka guidelines (precursor)
Apparel Export Promotion Council v. A.K. Chopra (1999) 1 SCC 759 — Sexual harassment doctrine
Medha Kotwal Lele v. Union of India (2013) 1 SCC 297 — Vishaka enforcement
Punjab and Sind Bank v. Durgesh Kuwar (2020) 18 SCC 644 — POSH Act application
Anita Suresh v. Union of India (2019) — Malicious complaint test
Initiating Department v. Anita Suresh — Service rules application after POSH inquiry
